_about: Applicant-facing wording (Decisions 30, 31, 33). Single source of truth for the API (serving/app.py), the dashboard (dashboard/scoring.py) and the public site (website/public/assets/reasons.js). The applicant sees an outcome (approved, or needs a manual review; never declined), the details of their own that counted, details to check, and model-tested changes. Model issues and the review cutoff are never shown to the applicant; they are in the risk officer output.

approved.headline: Your application has been approved
approved.summary: Based on the information you provided, the repayments appear affordable and your application met our approval criteria.
approved.why_none: Your overall financial position supported the decision.
next_steps: Your first repayment is taken today at checkout, then one every 30 days as shown in the plan.
Check the repayment amounts and dates before you accept the agreement.
This is a demonstration on synthetic data. It is not a real credit decision or financial advice.

manual_review.headline: Your application needs a manual review
manual_review.summary: We could not make an automatic decision, so a risk officer will review your application before a final decision is made. It has not been declined.
manual_review.why_intro: What counted against an automatic approval:
manual_review.why_none: No single detail stood out. A risk officer will look at the application as a whole.
next_steps: A risk officer will review your application and the details you gave.
If any detail is wrong, ask for it to be corrected before the review.
This is a demonstration on synthetic data. It is not a real credit decision or financial advice.

declined.headline: We cannot approve this application
declined.summary: On the figures you gave, the repayments would not be affordable.
next_steps: You can apply again with a smaller order or a longer repayment plan.
If any figure you gave is wrong, correct it and apply again: the outcome could be different.
This is a demonstration on synthetic data. It is not a real credit decision or financial advice.

changes_text.intro: Each of these on its own, with everything else the same, would have led to an automatic approval:
changes_text.none: No single change to the order, the repayment plan, your existing commitments or your savings would be enough on its own. A risk officer will look at the application as a whole.
changes_text.note: These changes do not guarantee approval. A future application will be assessed on your circumstances at that time.
changes_text.declined_intro: Each of these on its own would bring the repayments within our affordability limit:

method.new: Each detail was compared with a typical applicant by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.
method.existing: Each detail was compared with a typical customer by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.

status_detail.refer: The risk score is at or above the review line.
status_detail.divergence: The risk score alone would approve this, but a check below needs a person to look first.
status_detail.clear: Nothing needs a person. The application can be approved automatically.
status_detail.declined: The repayments are over the affordability limit, so the application is declined automatically.

review_reasons.refer: Estimated chance of falling 90 or more days behind on repayments: {pd}, at or above the {cutoff} review line.
review_reasons.data_input: Some details do not fit together or are outside the normal range: {issues}.
review_reasons.missing_information: Established credit file, but riskier than {pct}% of similar applicants. The risk score rarely flags this group on its own, so a person should check it.
review_reasons.overreliance: The decision rests almost entirely on one factor: {name}.
review_reasons.unaffordable: Not affordable: commitments of {obligations} a month plus the {instalment} instalment take {ratio} of income ({income}), above the {limit} limit.

affordability.triggered: No: {ratio} of income, above the {limit} limit.

data_input.name: Details make sense together

unexpected._about: risk_when on each field is the conventional credit-risk expectation (a declared assumption, Decision 34). When the model's effect runs the other way, the officer is told.
unexpected.against: {factor}. Unusually, the model counts this against the application
unexpected.favour: {factor}. Unusually, the model counts this in the application's favour

record.approver_note: Not recorded: the approval gate does not capture approver identity (Decision 23).
lineage: Decision 27: champion {model_version}, promoted on validity grounds
Decision 27: business cutoff {cutoff}, PD at or above it refers for review
Decision 30: plain-English reasons, one input at a time against a typical applicant
Decision 31: error-type checks and risk officer flag (rules {rules_version})
Decision 33: applicant outcome (approved or manual review), own-detail reasons, model-tested changes
Decision 34: thin-file status worked out automatically; plain-language risk officer view
Decision 35: affordability limit {limit} (FCA CONC 5.2A ratio); over it the application is declined
